newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds ended a slow day little changed from their previous closing levels as the market awaited U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the Senate budget committee.
The speech -- to be made at the committee's hearing on the U.S. economy and broadcast after local markets close -- would provide direction on Wednesday morning, bond traders said.
At 1415 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was yielding 15.63 percent from 15.60 percent late on Monday.
"The outcome of the Greenspan testimony and local trade figures (due from Thursday) are going to provide direction over the next couple of days," a bond trader said.
He said local and offshore selling around the 15.65 percent level had been balanced by buying from both quarters and it had been a dull day on the local bond market.
"The 15.65 percent level is providing a barrier on the upside while 15.50 percent is the next big level on the downside," the trader added.
Others said the high money-market shortage -- still persistently hovering above the 10 billion rand mark -- was preventing a significant move below the 15.50 percent level.
"Worries over the the high shortage are starting to filter through to the bond market but sentiment is still positive," a second trader commented.
The Reserve Bank said South Africa's money-market shortage rose slightly to 10.446 billion rand on Monday from 10.403 billion on Saturday.
But leading banks quoted their three-month NCD rates steady at between 17.25-17.50 percent while 90-day BA rates were also unchanged at 16.60-16.85 percent.

Foreigners bought a net 74.33 million rands' worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 142.28 million on Friday, the Bond Exchange said. Nominal cumulative turnover was 4.03 billion rand on Monday, it said.
On the currency market the rand edged slightly weaker against the U.S. dollar on the back of "tiny" dollar demand which was met by exporter dollar sales in orderly trade, a forex trader said.
It closed at 4.6520/6570 on the U.S. unit from 4.6400/6450 at the Monday close.
Traders said there was some concern over Greenspan's speech and Deputy President Thabo Mbeki's decision on a three billion rand arms sale to Syria, expected at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
A few dealers said there was room for the rand to strengthen to 4.63 on the dollar by the end of the week, anticipating a 4.63 to 4.67 range for the week.
Nedcor Ltd subsidiary UAL Merchant Bank Limited senior manager of international treasury, Neal Anderson, said the currency's recent stability appeared set to continue in the short-term.

"The rand has now held below the 4.70 close on the dollar for around five weeks, which indicates a good period of stability," he said, adding that speculators were reluctant to take on the unit on the upside.
"Sentiment has not totally changed but the rand has done very well against the stronger dollar," he noted.
A lot of importers had covered positions over the last few weeks and this, coupled with exporter dollar sales over Christmas and after the New Year, had helped the currency.

On the crosses, the rand was last trading weaker at 7.7519/7649 on sterling from 7.7108/7238 on Monday when it hit a five-week high. It was steady at 0.3486/3490 on the mark from Monday's 0.3496/3502 when it stormed to a six-month high.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
